narrative.text: Title page, publication metadata, and opening abstract for The PROV-JSONLD Serialization (W3C Member Submission, 25 August 2024), edited by Luc Moreau and Dong Huynh (King's College London), introducing PROV-JSONLD as a JSON serialization of PROV-DM with a JSON-LD semantic mapping for Web and Linked Data interchange.

Continuation of the abstract listing companion artifacts (`schema.json`, `context.jsonld`, and `provext.ttl`), the W3C Status of This Document section noting the King's College London Member Submission status and W3C Patent Policy terms, and the start of the Table of Contents (Sections 1–3).

Continuation of the Table of Contents covering Section 4 (Schema, subsections 4.1–4.20 for preliminary definitions, core PROV types, bundles, documents, and contexts) and Section 5 (JSON-LD Context, subsections 5.1–5.15).

Completion of the Table of Contents (Sections 5.16–6 and Appendices A–E), Section 1 (Conformance) specifying BCP 14 (RFC 2119 and RFC 8174) keyword interpretation, and the start of Section 2 (Introduction) reviewing 2013 W3C PROV serializations (PROV-N, PROV-XML, and PROV-O).

Continuation of Section 2 (Introduction) formulating four core serialization requirements—Lightweight, Natural, Semantic, and Efficient—evaluating why existing PROV-JSON, PROV-O RDF, PROV-XML, and PROV-N representations fail to satisfy all four simultaneously, and explaining how JSON-LD contextual mappings address the gap.

Conclusion of Section 2 summarizing how PROV-JSONLD satisfies the four requirements via self-contained JSON objects and JSON-LD 1.1 contextual mappings, followed by Section 2.1 (Namespace) and Table 1 defining the `prov`, `provext`, `xsd`, `rdf`, and example namespace prefixes.

Section 3 (Example, non-normative) introducing a subset of the PROV-PRIMER scenario (Figure 1, where agent Derek composes `article1` from `dataSet1`) and explaining how a top-level PROV-JSONLD document structures `@context` and `@graph` arrays of typed (`@type`) and optionally identified (`@id`) PROV expressions.

Continuation of Section 3 explaining how PROV expressions combine predefined properties (such as `activity` and `agent`), optional multi-valued `type` arrays, and prefixed external attributes (such as `foaf:givenName`), while requiring a single-valued `@type` property for fast parser dispatch.

First part of Example 1 showing a complete PROV-JSONLD document with its `@context` declarations (`xsd`, `dcterms`, `ex`, `prov`, `foaf`, and the canonical `context.jsonld` URI) and `@graph` entries for `Entity` (`ex:dataSet1`, `ex:article1`), `Derivation`, `Agent` (`ex:derek`), `Association`, `Activity` (`ex:compose`), and the start of `Usage`.

Completion of Example 1 (`Usage` and `Generation` objects), the introduction to Section 4 (Schema), and the start of Section 4.1 (Preliminary Definitions) specifying the JSON Schema definitions for `DateTime` and `QualifiedName`.

Continuation of Section 4.1 completing the `QualifiedName` regex pattern with an editor's note on post-processor validation against PROV-N production rules, followed by the JSON Schema definitions for `typed_value` (`@value` and `@type`) and `lang_string` (`@value` and optional `@language`).

Completion of Section 4.1 defining `ArrayOfValues` and `ArrayOfLabelValues`, and the start of Section 4.2 (`prov:Entity`) specifying the required `@id` and `@type` (`Entity`) properties and optional `type`, `location`, and `label` attributes.

JSON Schema definition for `prov:Entity` (requiring `@type` and `@id`, with optional `type`, `value`, `location`, `label`, and prefixed `patternProperties`), followed by Section 4.3 (`prov:Activity`) specifying required and optional activity properties (`startTime`, `endTime`, `type`, `location`, `label`).

Completion of the JSON Schema definition for `prov:Activity`, followed by Section 4.4 (`prov:Agent`) and its JSON Schema definition requiring `@type` (`Agent`) and `@id` and permitting `type`, `location`, `label`, and prefixed extension properties.

Section 4.5 (`prov:Derivation`) specifying the schema for derivations—requiring `@type` (`Derivation`), recommending `generatedEntity` and `usedEntity`, and permitting `@id`, `activity`, `generation`, `usage`, `type`, `label`, and prefixed properties.

Section 4.6 (`prov:Attribution`) specifying the JSON Schema for attribution expressions—requiring `@type` (`Attribution`), recommending `entity` and `agent`, and allowing optional `@id`, `type`, `label`, and prefixed attributes.

Section 4.7 (`prov:Association`) specifying the JSON Schema for activity-agent associations—requiring `@type` (`Association`), recommending `activity` and `agent`, and allowing optional `@id`, `plan`, `location`, `role`, `type`, `label`, and prefixed properties.

Section 4.8 (`prov:Delegation`) specifying the JSON Schema for agent delegation—requiring `@type` (`Delegation`), recommending `delegate` and `responsible`, and allowing optional `@id`, `activity`, `type`, `label`, and prefixed properties.

Section 4.9 (`prov:Usage`) specifying the JSON Schema for activity entity usage—requiring `@type` (`Usage`), recommending `activity` and `entity`, and allowing optional `@id`, `time`, `location`, `role`, `type`, `label`, and prefixed properties.

Section 4.10 (`prov:Generation`) specifying the JSON Schema for entity generation—requiring `@type` (`Generation`), recommending `entity` and `activity`, and allowing optional `@id`, `time`, `location`, `role`, `type`, `label`, and prefixed properties.

Section 4.11 (`prov:Invalidation`) specifying the JSON Schema for entity invalidation—requiring `@type` (`Invalidation`), recommending `entity` and `activity`, and allowing optional `@id`, `time`, `location`, `role`, `type`, `label`, and prefixed properties.

Section 4.12 (`prov:Start`) specifying the JSON Schema for activity start events—requiring `@type` (`Start`), recommending `activity`, and allowing optional `starter`, `trigger`, `@id`, `time`, `location`, `role`, `type`, `label`, and prefixed properties.

Section 4.13 (`prov:End`) specifying the JSON Schema for activity end events—requiring `@type` (`End`), recommending `activity`, and allowing optional `ender`, `trigger`, `@id`, `time`, `location`, `role`, `type`, `label`, and prefixed properties.

Section 4.14 (`prov:Communication`) specifying the JSON Schema for activity communication (`@type` `Communication`, recommended `informed` and `informant`, optional `@id`, `type`, `label`, and prefixed properties), and the start of Section 4.15 (`prov:Influence`).

Completion of Section 4.15 (`prov:Influence`) with its JSON Schema (`@type` `Influence`, recommended `influencer` and `influencee`), followed by the prose of Section 4.16 (`prov:Specialization`) describing `specificEntity`, `generalEntity`, and optional extension properties.

JSON Schema definition for `prov:Specialization` (Section 4.16), followed by Section 4.17 (`prov:Alternate`) specifying required `@type` (`Alternate`), recommended `alternate1` and `alternate2`, and optional `@id`, `type`, `label`, and prefixed properties.

Completion of the JSON Schema for `prov:Alternate`, followed by Section 4.18 (`prov:Membership`) and its JSON Schema requiring `@type` (`Membership`), recommending `collection` and `entity` (single or array), and allowing optional `@id`, `type`, `label`, and prefixed properties.

Completion of the `prov:Membership` schema and the `QualifiedName+` helper definition (single `QualifiedName` or array), followed by Section 4.19 (`prov:Bundle` and `prov:Document`) and the start of the `prov:Bundle` JSON Schema.
Completion of the `prov:Bundle` and `prov:Document` JSON Schemas (requiring `@context` and `@graph`), followed by the prose and opening schema for `prov:Statement` and `prov:StatementOrBundle`.
Completion of the `prov:Statement` and `prov:StatementOrBundle` union schemas, followed by Section 4.20 (`Context`) introducing the JSON Schema for `@context` arrays.

Completion of the `Context` JSON Schema (URI strings or prefix-mapping objects), followed by Section 5 (JSON-LD Context) and Section 5.1 (Introduction: Qualification Pattern) explaining how PROV-O qualifies binary influence relations using intermediate classes.

First part of Figure 2 (adapted from PROV-O), diagramming the RDF Qualification Pattern classes and properties for Usage (a), Generation (b), Invalidation (c), Communication (d), Start (e), End (f), Derivation (g), and Attribution (i).

Completion of Figure 2 showing Delegation (h), Attribution (i), and Association (j) qualification patterns, followed by Section 5.2 (Default and generic Context Elements) defining default JSON-LD `@id` mappings for `entity` (`prov:entity`), `activity` (`prov:activity`), and `agent` (`prov:agent`).

Continuation of Section 5.2 defining context-invariant mappings for `role` (`prov:hadRole`), `type` (`rdf:type`), `label` (`rdfs:label`), and `location` (`prov:atLocation`), followed by Section 5.3 (Entity) mapping `Entity` to `prov:Entity` and its scoped `value` property to `prov:value`.

Section 5.4 (Activity) defining the scoped JSON-LD context for `Activity` (`startTime` to `prov:startedAtTime` and `endTime` to `prov:endedAtTime` with `xsd:dateTime` coercion) and Section 5.5 (Agent) mapping `Agent` to `prov:Agent` with an empty local context.

Section 5.6 (Derivation) defining the scoped JSON-LD context for `Derivation` (`prov:Derivation`), mapping `generatedEntity` via `@reverse` `prov:qualifiedDerivation` and mapping `usedEntity`, `generation`, `activity`, and `usage` to `prov:entity`, `prov:hadGeneration`, `prov:hadActivity`, and `prov:hadUsage`.

Section 5.7 (Attribution) defining the scoped JSON-LD context for `Attribution` (`entity` mapped via `@reverse` `prov:qualifiedAttribution`) and the start of Section 5.8 (Association) mapping `activity` via `@reverse` `prov:qualifiedAssociation` and `plan` to `prov:hadPlan`.

Completion of the Section 5.8 `Association` context, followed by Section 5.9 (Delegation) defining the scoped JSON-LD context for `Delegation` (`responsible` to `prov:agent`, `delegate` via `@reverse` `prov:qualifiedDelegation`, and `activity` to `prov:hadActivity`).

Section 5.10 (Usage) defining the scoped JSON-LD context for `Usage` (`activity` via `@reverse` `prov:qualifiedUsage` and `time` to `prov:atTime` as `xsd:dateTime`), followed by the start of Section 5.11 (Generation).

Completion of Section 5.11 (`Generation` context mapping `entity` via `@reverse` `prov:qualifiedGeneration` and `time` to `prov:atTime`), followed by Section 5.12 (Invalidation) mapping `entity` via `@reverse` `prov:qualifiedInvalidation` and `time` to `prov:atTime` (`xsd:dateTime`).

Section 5.13 (Start) defining the scoped JSON-LD context for `Start` (`activity` via `@reverse` `prov:qualifiedStart`, `trigger` to `prov:entity`, `starter` to `prov:hadActivity`, and `time` to `prov:atTime`), followed by the prose introduction to Section 5.14 (End).

Completion of Section 5.14 (`End` context mapping `activity` via `@reverse` `prov:qualifiedEnd`, `trigger` to `prov:entity`, `ender` to `prov:hadActivity`, and `time` to `prov:atTime`), followed by the prose introduction to Section 5.15 (Communication).

JSON-LD context for `Communication` (Section 5.15, mapping `informed` via `@reverse` `prov:qualifiedCommunication` and `informant` to `prov:activity`), followed by Section 5.16 (Influence) mapping `influencee` via `@reverse` `prov:qualifiedInfluence` and `influencer` to `prov:influencer`.

Section 5.17 (Specialization) explaining the `provext` qualification extension for `Specialization` (`specificEntity` via `@reverse` `provext:qualifiedSpecialization` and `generalEntity` to `provext:generalEntity`), followed by the opening of Section 5.18 (Alternate).

Completion of Section 5.18 (`Alternate` context in `provext`, mapping `alternate1` via `@reverse` `provext:qualifiedAlternate` and `alternate2` to `provext:alternate`), followed by the prose of Section 5.19 (Membership) introducing `provext:qualifiedMembership` and `provext:member`.

JSON-LD context for `Membership` (Section 5.19) using `provext:Membership`, followed by Section 6 (Interoperability Considerations) covering IC1 (relaxing entity/activity presence to `SHOULD` for incomplete provenance) and the start of IC2 (qualifying binary relations).

Continuation of Section 6 completing IC2 (`provext` qualification classes for `Specialization`, `Alternate`, and `Membership`), presenting IC3 (document root object carrying `@context`), and introducing IC4 (encoding PROV subtypes and subrelations via `prov:type`).

Completion of IC4 with a JSON-LD snippet illustrating `prov:Person` and `prov:Revision` inside `type`, followed by IC5 specifying two roundtrip interoperability test protocols (Java-to-PROV-JSONLD-to-Java and Java-to-PROV-JSONLD-to-Turtle-to-Java) implemented in ProvToolbox.

Completion of Section 6 (IC5) with GitHub links to the two ProvToolbox JUnit roundtrip test classes, followed by the opening of Appendix A (JSON Schema for PROV-JSONLD) defining `DateTime`, `QualifiedName`, `QualifiedName+`, and `non_prov_properties`.
Continuation of Appendix A listing the full JSON Schema definitions for `typed_value`, `lang_string`, `ArrayOfValues`, and the start of `ArrayOfLabelValues`.
Continuation of Appendix A defining the `Context`, `prov:StatementOrBundle`, and `prov:Statement` union schemas in the consolidated PROV-JSONLD JSON Schema.
Continuation of Appendix A completing `prov:Statement` and listing the full JSON Schema definitions for `prov:Entity`, `prov:Agent`, and the beginning of `prov:Activity`.
Continuation of Appendix A completing `prov:Activity` and listing the full JSON Schema definitions for `prov:Usage` and `prov:Generation`.
Continuation of Appendix A completing `prov:Generation` and listing the full JSON Schema definitions for `prov:Invalidation` and `prov:Start`.
Continuation of Appendix A listing the full JSON Schema definitions for `prov:End` and `prov:Attribution`.
Continuation of Appendix A listing the full JSON Schema definitions for `prov:Association`, `prov:Delegation`, and the start of `prov:Derivation`.
Continuation of Appendix A completing `prov:Derivation` and listing the full JSON Schema definitions for `prov:Alternate` and the start of `prov:Specialization`.
Continuation of Appendix A completing `prov:Specialization` and listing the full JSON Schema definitions for `prov:Membership` and `prov:Influence`.
Continuation of Appendix A listing the full JSON Schema definitions for `prov:Communication`, `prov:Bundle`, and the start of `prov:Document`.

Completion of Appendix A (`prov:Document` and top-level `$schema`, `$id`, and `$ref` declarations for `https://openprovenance.org/prov-jsonld/schema.json`), followed by the start of Appendix B (JSON-LD Context for PROV-JSONLD) declaring `@version: 1.1`, namespace prefixes, and generic term definitions (`role`, `type`, `label`, `location`).
Continuation of Appendix B listing the consolidated JSON-LD 1.1 context definitions for `entity`, `activity`, `agent`, `Activity`, `Entity`, `Agent`, and the start of `Delegation`.
Continuation of Appendix B listing the consolidated JSON-LD 1.1 scoped contexts for `Delegation`, `Usage`, and `Generation`.
Continuation of Appendix B listing the consolidated JSON-LD 1.1 scoped contexts for `Invalidation`, `Attribution`, and `Association`.
Continuation of Appendix B listing the consolidated JSON-LD 1.1 scoped contexts for `Communication`, `Influence`, and the start of `Derivation`.
Continuation of Appendix B completing `Derivation` and listing the consolidated JSON-LD 1.1 scoped contexts for `Start` and the beginning of `End`.
Continuation of Appendix B completing `End` and listing the consolidated JSON-LD 1.1 scoped contexts for `Specialization` and `Membership` in the `provext` namespace.

Completion of Appendix B (`Alternate` context in `provext`), followed by the start of Appendix C (PROVEXT: PROV Ontology Extension for PROV-JSONLD) presenting the Turtle OWL 2 ontology header and top object property declarations for `https://openprovenance.org/ns/provext#`.

Continuation of Appendix C defining the `provext` OWL object properties (`:qualifiedMembership`, `:qualifiedSpecialization`, `:qualifiedAlternate`, `:member`, `:generalEntity`, `:alternate`) with their domains and ranges, plus the `:Membership`, `:Alternate`, and `:Specialization` OWL classes.

Completion of Appendix C defining OWL property chain axioms (`prov:specializationOf`, `prov:alternateOf`, and `prov:hadMember`), Appendix D (Acknowledgements thanking Pierre-Antoine Champin and Denis Ah-Kang), and the start of Appendix E.1 (Normative references: JSON-LD, JSON-LD 1.1, and JSON-SCHEMA).
Continuation of Appendix E.1 (Normative references) listing citations for LINKED-DATA, PROV-DM, PROV-N, PROV-O, PROV-XML, RDF-CONCEPTS, RFC 2119, RFC 3987, RFC 8174, RFC 8259, and XMLSCHEMA11-2.
Appendix E.2 (Informative references) listing citations for the IPAW'16 PROV-JSONLD poster, the 2013 PROV-JSON Member Submission, PROV-Overview, and the PROV Model Primer.
